title: B sends a negative offset to the expenses LIST
must_not: return any row belonging to A, in the body, in an error message, or in a count
source: P-REC-02 — a negative offset is malformed input. The title previously read "A's summary with a manipulated cursor"; the summary has no cursor, offset or pagination of any kind (CV-07 fixes its parameters at from, to, category_id, uncategorised). Following the title would have meant inventing a pagination model for the summary

title: B attempts A's list with a manipulated sort

must_not: return any row belonging to A, in the body, in an error message, or in a count
source: P-REC-02 — the sort allowlist is closed; SW-ADR-038

title: B attempts A's list with an id array

must_not: return any row belonging to A, in the body, in an error message, or in a count

title: an admin's own summary silently totals everyone's spending
persona: ADMIN (who is also a person with their own expenses)

must_not: include any other person's row in the total, the count, or by_category
source: SW-ADR-129 — the superseded SW-ADR-077 policy made this fail silently and NO stated test covered it. This case exists because of that gap

title: redeeming a reset token issued for another person
request: POST /api/auth/reset/complete with a token issued for A
expected_status: the reset applies to A ONLY
expected_body: ONLY A's password changes and ONLY A's sessions are revoked. B's password and B's live sessions survive untouched
must_not: change B's password; revoke B's sessions; apply A's token to the caller's account
source: SW-ADR-134 — the account-takeover surface, and the endpoint the narrow wording would have excluded
